newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Third group lines up for Singapore telecom licence.
newsitem.headline: Third group lines up for Singapore telecom licence.

text.p: Competition to run basic telecommunications services in Singapore heated up Monday with a third consortium announcing it was considering bidding for a licence.

Diversified maritime conglomerate SembCorp Ltd and Singapore MRT Ltd, which runs Singapore's train system, said they were contemplating entering the race for a licence together as the domestic part of a bidding consortium.

"The consortium is currently evaluating the terms and conditions as well as the overall feasibility of bidding for the licence. The consortium is also in discussion with potential foreign telephone companies who may be invited to joint the consortium in the bid," the companies said in a joint statement.

Singapore plans to open up its telecoms market to competition from April, 2000, and has said it will licence one or two new groups to compete directly with the current monopoly, Singapore Telecommunications Ltd, from that date.
SembCorp and Singapore MRT, which is owned by state investment company Temasek Holdings, are the third group of companies to signal their interest in bidding for a licence.

On March 13, British Telecommunications Ltd (BT), Nippon Telegraph and Telephone Corp (NTT) and two other Temasek-owned companies, state utility Singapore Power (SP) and Singapore Technologies Telemedia (STT), said they formed a consortium to bid for a licence.

The island's newspaper monopoly, Singapore Press Holdings, and Keppel Telecommunications and Transportation Ltd have also said they want to bid in partnership, as has Britain's Cable & Wireless (CW) and its unit Hong Kong Telecommunications (HK Tel).
Analysts greeted the SembCorp/MRT announcement with interest but said it did not, on the face of it, appear quite as strong a consortium as the group formed by BT, NTT, SP and STT.
"It doesn't look as strong a proposition as the consortium formed last week for several reasons," said Gautam Kapoor, Asian regional telecommunications analyst for ING-Barings.

"That group included the very strong weight provided by BT and NTT, and secondly, STT already has a telecoms infrastructure in Singapore through its 24 percent ownership of Singapore Cablevision. Singapore Power also has power lines," Kapoor added.
"So its interesting, but we will have to see who will join them from overseas," he said.

Apart from CW and HK Tel, analysts say AT & T of the United States is probably considering joining a consortium for a Singapore licence as is the Global One alliance of Sprint Corp of the United States, France Telecom and Deutsche Telekom AG.

Analysts say a successful bid for a licence could involve an initial investment outlay of US$500 million to $1 billion. The cost involved would depend on the amount of existing infrastructure the group could use, they said.
